note: THE FIRST CHICAGO DIRECTORY, and it is nine years later than this reconstruction's scene date. An entry here is evidence about 1844 and never on its own an 1835 fact: it can corroborate that a person attested in 1835 was still in the city, and it can supply a trade or a street that the 1835 record lacks, said as 1844 evidence. The owner asked for it on 2026-09-03 at HathiTrust chi.56111136 (a 1933 reprint); that copy sits behind a Cloudflare challenge this runner cannot pass, and the volume was read instead from the University of Illinois scan of the 1903 Bohan republication on the Internet Archive, which is the same 1844 text. The reading is transcription_mediated: archive.org's OCR of the printed page, not checked against the image by eye. Read at the IMAGE in three places since: T-0903 and T-0900 for four garbled forenames, and T-0987 stretch 10 for the twenty-five surnames the independent second reading disagreed about (sixteen repaired, two upheld against that second hand, seven left to T-1018's firm-conjunction ruling). Each of those rows carries its own leaf, leaf size and djvu word box, so the crop can be reproduced; the rest of the volume is still the OCR.
